# `Config`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Config — typed TOML/YAML/JSON decoders.

A `Decoder a` describes how to extract a value of type `a` from a
config document.  Compose with `field` / `at` / `nullable` / `map`
/ `andThen`; run via `decodeToml` / `decodeYaml` / `decodeJson`
or `loadFromFile` (which detects the format by extension).

Shape mirrors `Ipe.Json.Decode` — code that already does
JSON decoding gets a consistent vocabulary for TOML and YAML.

Example:

    type alias DbCfg = { host : String, port : Int, name : String }

    dbDecoder : Decoder DbCfg
    dbDecoder =
        Config.succeed (\h p n -> { host = h, port = p, name = n })
            |> Config.andThen
                (\\f -> Config.map f (Config.field "host" Config.string))
            |> Config.andThen
                (\\f -> Config.map f (Config.field "port" Config.int))
            |> Config.andThen
                (\\f -> Config.map f (Config.field "name" Config.string))

    loadDb : Task Error DbCfg
    loadDb =
        case Path.fromString "config/database.toml" of
            Err e  -> Task.fail e
            Ok p   -> Config.loadFromFile p dbDecoder

```ipe
nullable : Decoder a -> Decoder (Maybe a)
```

`nullable decoder` — like `decoder`, but `Nothing` on null /

## `field`

```ipe
field : String -> Decoder a -> Decoder a
```

`field name decoder` — decode the named field at the current
level.  Fails if the field is missing or its value doesn't
match `decoder`.

## `at`

```ipe
at : List String -> Decoder a -> Decoder a
```

`at path decoder` — drill into nested fields.  `at ["db",
"host"] string` is equivalent to `field "db" (field "host"
string)`.

```ipe
list : Decoder a -> Decoder (List a)
```

## `index`

```ipe
index : Int -> Decoder a -> Decoder a
```

`index n decoder` — decode the n-th element of an array. Fails on
out-of-bounds or non-array input.

## `keyValuePairs`

```ipe
keyValuePairs : Decoder a -> Decoder (List ( String, a ))
```

`keyValuePairs decoder` — decode every entry of an object into a list of
`(key, value)` pairs, applying `decoder` to each value.

## `dict`

```ipe

```

`dict decoder` — decode an object into a `Dict String a`, applying
`decoder` to each value.

## `map2`

```ipe
map2 : (a -> b -> c) -> Decoder a -> Decoder b -> Decoder c
```

`map2`..`map8` — combine 2..8 decoders over the SAME value with an N-ary
function; the first failing decoder short-circuits. Load-bearing for record
decoding. Each shares the runtime `decode_mapN` (a captured `Decoder` cannot
be forwarded through a Rust closure — IPE-L0126 — so these are kernels, not
pure `andThen`/`map` compositions).

## `oneOf`

```ipe
oneOf : List (Decoder a) -> Decoder a
```

`oneOf decoders` — try each decoder in order, returning the first that
succeeds. Fails (with the last branch's error) if none match. Load-bearing
for decoding unions / heterogeneous shapes.

## `maybe`

```ipe
maybe : Decoder a -> Decoder (Maybe a)
```

`maybe decoder` — succeed with `Just` when `decoder` matches, else `Nothing`
(never fails). Unlike `nullable` (which only tolerates null/missing), `maybe`
catches ANY decode failure.

```ipe
decodeToml : String -> Decoder a -> Result Error a
```

Run a decoder against a TOML document.

## `decodeYaml`

```ipe
decodeYaml : String -> Decoder a -> Result Error a
```

Run a decoder against a YAML document.

The accepted YAML is a strict subset: exactly one document; YAML 1.2 core
booleans only (`true` / `false` in any letter case; `yes`, `no`, `on` and
`off` stay strings); `null` in any letter case, `~`, an empty value, and an
empty source are null; integers take `0x`, `0o` and `0b` prefixes; no
duplicate mapping keys, no merge keys (`<<`), and no tags beyond the core
schema (`!!str`, `!!int`, ...), so `!include` and local
tags are refused; no `.nan` or `.inf`; nesting at most 128 deep. A plain
leading-zero number such as `012` decodes as the number 12; quote it to keep
the string. A source past `IPE_YAML_MAX_BYTES`, or past a parser ceiling
(nesting depth, node count, anchor and alias expansion), is an `Err` of kind
`LimitExceeded`; every other refusal names its class and position, never
the source text.

## `decodeJson`

```ipe
decodeJson : String -> Decoder a -> Result Error a
```

Run a decoder against a JSON document.  Alias for
`Ipe.Json.Decode.decodeString` from the Config namespace.

## `loadFromFile`

```ipe
loadFromFile : Path -> Decoder a -> Task Error a
```

`loadFromFile path decoder` — read `path` (a validated `Path`,
NUL-byte- and `..`-traversal-checked), dispatch to the right
decoder by extension (`.toml`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`), then
decode.  Use `Path.fromString` to obtain a `Path` from a raw string.
